title: The first peopling of Sahul, c. 65,000–50,000 years ago
summary: With the sea more than 100 metres lower than today, Australia and New Guinea were one continent, Sahul, but the islands of Wallacea still lay between it and Asia. People crossed between 50,000 and 65,000 years ago. Two routes are proposed: an island chain between Sulawesi and New Guinea, and a way to north-western Australia by Timor. Both are drawn; neither is recorded.

events.label: Madjedbebe, Arnhem Land
events.text: A rock shelter with the oldest dated signs of people in Australia: possibly by 65,000 ± 6,000 years ago, and at least by 50,000. A 2020 study argued termites had moved the dated layers and questioned the older date; Clarkson's team stands by it.
